To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynamic annotation of the PTB is a very promising task and that the disambiguation techniques we use in this paper are useful and can be used in a wide variety of annotation projects.

the ERG can be successfully used to annotate compound nouns and the resulting annotation can be disambiguated in a way that is consistent with the grammar and the semantics, and that the disambiguation can be done automatically.

the ERG is a very good grammar of English, and that the WSJ section of the PTB is a very good corpus of English, and thus the combination of these two resources, the ERG-WSJ, is an excellent resource for linguistic annotation, which can be further enriched with semantic and discourse information, as well as with information about the internal (syndactic) structure of compound nouns, which can be used for the purpose of disambiguation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How can the internal structure of compound nouns be represented in a treebank?
the following issues: (1) How to disambiguate compound nouns in the PTB?
the annotation and disambiguation task of English compound nouns in the context of a large-scale and wide coverage treebank.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the disambiguation techniques and methods proposed in this paper are of great importance in the context of the dynamic annotation of WSJ texts, as they help in the annotation task, and also facilitate the creation of a truly sharable and re-usable resource.

the annotation process of the WSJ texts with the help of the ERG is a very challenging and complex one, since it requires the annotation of the texts with the help not only of a very large-scale grammar, but also with the help of an equally large-scale lexicon, which in turn requires a very careful and detailed analysis of the internal structure of the words in the corpus.

the annotation of compound nouns in the PTB is a task which is of great interest for the linguistic annotation of large-scale corpora, and that the disambiguation techniques presented in this paper are useful and necessary for this purpose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the annotation of compound nouns is an interesting task in its own right and that it is a task that can be done with high accuracy, but that the accuracy is highly sensitive to the quality and the quantity of the linguistic resources that are used for disambiguation.

we have developed and tested methods for dynamically annotating compound nouns, which are based on disambiguation techniques and which are implemented within the ERG framework, and we have shown the impact that the annotation of compound nouns has on the semantic annotation of the WSJ texts of the PTB.
we propose and evaluate a set of disambiguation techniques for compound nouns, based on a number of linguistic features, which are used to disambiguate their internal syntactic structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in general, the annotation of a corpus with the help of an HPSG grammar can be a very useful tool for the disambiguation task of the internal structure of compounds, since it can provide a better understanding of their semantics.

the ERG is a powerful tool which can facilitate the annotation of a treebank, since it is able to provide a wide-coverage and linguistically rich description of the linguistic data, but also that it needs to be complemented with a number of disambiguation techniques, in order to make it more efficient.
the annotation of compound nouns can be done dynamically and in a linguistically motivated manner.
